title: Elementary particles are persistent localized structures in the network

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Elementary particles are persistent localized structures in the network

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Elementary particles are analogs of the localized structures seen in class 4 cellular automata: persistent structures (such as tangles or non-planar cores) in the network of space, so that the fundamental rules need make no reference to particular particles.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: An immediate possibility that I suspect is actually not too far from the mark is that such particles are analogs of the localized structures that we saw earlier in this book in systems like the class 4 cellular automata shown below.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Elementary Particles” (from p. 525), p. 525. Scope: elementary particles of physics

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-22: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.41

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Observed particle properties provide a demanding comparison target, and candidate rules can be simulated. The missing rule and absence of distinctive microscopic observations prevent resolution of the ontological claim today.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Specify a network dynamics, enumerate its persistent localized structures, and derive their masses, charges, spins, interactions, and scattering signatures. A stable spectrum matching observed particles without particle-specific rules would support the claim; failure to reproduce those properties would refute that model.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No specific fundamental network rule is given.

Many localized structures can be engineered without matching particle phenomenology.

Existing data do not reveal substructure at the proposed scale.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.22
discriminating power: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.48
analysis feasibility: 0.3

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Particle properties are catalogued in detail, and localized structures in class 4 rules are easy to simulate. Neither resource connects a persistent network tangle to an electron or a quark. The claim stays a hypothesis until a model produces the spectrum, and no such public dataset exists.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Identify persistent localized structures in a network model of space and match their conserved attributes and interaction rules to the elementary-particle spectrum. A one-to-one match with no particle-specific rules would support the claim; a spectrum that cannot be realized by persistent network structures would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Solitons, strings, and other localized-structure models fit the same particle data.

Resemblance to class 4 gliders does not test whether physical particles are network tangles.

discriminating power: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.4
